reviewed_behaviors.behavior: rejected password preserves old credentials and rejects the candidate
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The security form has uniquely labeled password inputs “Current password”, “New password”, and “Confirm password”, and a button “Update password”; submitting an empty current-password field must display the visible application message “Current password is required”. A failure with an incorrect current password and confirmation “does-not-match” must display the corresponding current-password or confirmation error and leave the old credentials usable. Each password-change scenario starts with its own verified account in the stated credential state and a different compliant candidate password. “Password and authentication” is the security page in account Settings used to change the current account credentials; the change affects only the current account's password record and does not alter any other accounts or resources outside the session. The user must provide the current password, a new password compliant with the REQ-1 password rules, and a character-for-character identical confirmation password; all three fields are required. The system validates the change, prevents unauthorized updates, and applies the new password to subsequent sign-in attempts. If the current password is incorrect, the new password is noncompliant, the confirmation does not match, or any field is missing, the system displays the reason in the corresponding field and does not modify the credentials; the applicable visible message is “Current password is incorrect”, “Password confirmation does not match”, or “Current password is required”. The old password remains valid and the new password must not work for sign-in. After a successful update, the page displays “Password updated”, the new password is immediately used for subsequent password-based sign-ins, and the old password must no longer work for new sign-ins.

Seed password-change values are `New-password-456!` for the successful update and
`Required-password-789!` for the missing-current-password scenario.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-password-settings.png)

exported_witnesses.title: REQ-1-3: missing current password and mismatch leave original credentials usable

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: private team grant changes access, preserves outsider denial and is idempotent
reviewed_behaviors.basis: From the repository's “Settings” link, open the “Manage access” link and activate “Add people or teams”. The picker presents a textbox “Search”, a matching selectable team option whose name contains the team name, a combobox “Role” with clickable role options including “Write”, and an “Add” button. While the picker is active, hide the opening Add people or teams button from the active view so the submit action is unambiguous. After saving, the authorization list visibly shows the exact team name and Write role and retains the team after reload. Existing grants appear as rows whose accessible names include the subject name; each row contains a native select labeled “Role” and a “Save” button. Selecting the option labeled “Read” and saving replaces Write; after reload exactly one row for the team remains and contains Read. The creation scenario supplies a repository Admin and an organization team not yet granted access; the replacement scenario supplies a separate repository/team with an existing Write grant. An organization Owner or repository Admin may grant a repository role of Read, Triage, Write, Maintain, or Admin to a current organization member or team. In the access-subject picker, matching member or team options update as the administrator types; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. A private repository is accessible only to an organization Owner, a member with a direct repository role, or a direct member of a team that has a repository role; an ordinary organization Member has no default private-repository access. For a given subject and repository, only one direct role grant is stored — saving the same role again does not create a second record, and changing the role replaces the original role. An account's effective repository role is the highest among Admin from Owner status and all still-valid direct grants and team grants; team hierarchy does not propagate membership or authorization. The system stores the authorization subject, repository, role, grantor, and timestamp and authorizes operations according to the ROOT role matrix; unauthorized accounts cannot see private repositories. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication) and REQ-2-2-1 (Create an Organization Team); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: file history excludes unrelated commits; branch order persists
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Any user with repository-view permission can read branch history on the Commits page, or from a file page read only the history that modified that file; each record references the stored commit identifier, author, time, message, parent commit, and changed files. The repository and file pages each expose one history link named “Commits” (a commit count may accompany the visible label without introducing another matching link). Seed history includes a known commit message and author, displayed in full as distinct readable text values, and a relative timestamp containing “ago”. Opening the branch history directly from the repository must show these values without first selecting a file-specific scope.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: path/message boundaries and unauthorized creation preserve history
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-web-file-editor.png)

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: blank comment preserves loaded discussion; Read/Triage cannot comment
reviewed_behaviors.basis: Only a signed-in user with Write, Maintain, or Admin may enter a non-empty comment on the issue detail page of the current repository; all signed-in users who can view the issue may add or remove their own reactions on an existing issue or comment. The system stores the comment identifier, issue identifier, author, body, and creation time, or stores a “subject-target-reaction type” association; for the same user, target, and reaction, only one association is stored, and selecting it a second time removes it. On success, the new comment or reaction is displayed in the discussion and activity timeline; on failure, no local fake comment or partial reaction is displayed. The comment editor is labeled “Comment”, and its submit button is named exactly “Comment”. After submission the complete comment text and author username are visible, and the saved comment remains after reload. Discussion and activity entries use article semantics so an invalid submission cannot add an article; existing entries remain stable across reload. For whitespace-only text the Comment button may either be disabled or remain enabled and display “Comment is required” when activated. Neither path adds a comment or activity. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-5-1-2 (View an Issue and Its Discussion) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: PR milestone add/remove, cross-repository exclusion and role denial
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
On the right side of an issue or pull request, the user clicks the settings icon in the “Milestone” area and selects one item from the current repository's milestone list, or selects “None” to remove the association. The system stores the association between the work item and milestone and updates detail metadata; it does not create a cross-repository milestone. The settings icon is a button named “Milestone”, and selectable items have role option with the exact milestone name as their accessible name. Seed data provides a selectable milestone belonging to the current repository and an issue not yet associated with it. Clicking the option immediately saves the association and closes the picker with no separate confirmation or save action; the exact milestone name remains visible after reload. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-5-1-2 (View an Issue and Its Discussion); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Only users with Triage, Maintain, or Admin may use this capability on repository planning and issue-management pages; Read and Write users may only view the current milestone. The system validates the role and rejects unauthorized submissions.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: Open/Draft/Closed and a real merge-derived Merged filter
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
The Pull requests list page only reads PR records from the current repository; each row displays the number, title, author, status, source branch, and target branch. Any user with repository-view permission may filter by Draft/Open/Closed/Merged status, author, or review status; filtering only affects the current list display and does not modify PRs, branches, or reviews. The public list is directly accessible to a visitor and has an Open link for the status filter; selecting it displays the seeded Open PR as a link whose exact accessible name is its title. Opening that link displays the same title as a heading. After reloading the filtered list, that Open PR remains visible; leaving the page and reopening the list, then selecting Open again, shows the same PR. Seed data includes this public list and a stable, uniquely titled Open PR as well as the Closed PR and author used in the filtering scenario. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-3-3 (View a Public Repository Overview); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: author, Draft, Read and Triage cannot persist review decisions
reviewed_behaviors.basis: From the Files changed link, the reviewer activates the Review changes button to open one review form with an optional Summary field, radio controls named Comment, Approve, and Request changes, and a Submit review button. Selecting Approve and submitting without a summary is valid and displays Approved. Selecting Request changes with a summary displays Changes requested and that exact summary; the decision remains visible after reload. Seed data supplies a non-author Write reviewer and separate Open PRs for approval and request-changes submission, with no initial effective decision by that reviewer. A user who is not the PR author and has Write, Maintain, or Admin may submit Comment, Approve, or Request changes on an Open PR; the author and Draft PRs cannot submit reviews. The system stores the review decision, reviewer, current compare commit, optional explanation, and time; a new decision by the same reviewer replaces that reviewer's effective decision for the current commit while preserving the old record. Approve is valid only when the reviewer is not the author and the compare commit is still the same; Request changes blocks merging until that reviewer submits a new Comment or Approve for the current compare commit, or the compare branch receives a new commit that makes the old decision stale. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-1 (View Pull Request Overview and Commits) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: Write/Read/Triage cannot merge; failed required check blocks an approved PR
reviewed_behaviors.basis: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
